scope: PP4 Prefill stage (TP1/EP1, 24 layers), one microbatch of two requests. CPU compile, Triton interpreter and torch stand-in checks only; speed and exactness on H200 are decided by the in-job selection scripts/select-firmus-prefill-moe-input.py.

profile.file: prefill-0 nsys, stage 0 (device 0), kernels between consecutive MegaMoE calls of one microbatch

fused.change: post-attention add-RMSNorm (Triton, one row per program, 8 warps) writes the BF16 residual, BF16 y in place, FP8 x, FP32 row-major scales and the pad top-k slots of the MegaMoE buffer; the unchanged Triton router writes int64 ids and FP32 weights into the buffer; pre-dispatch is skipped
fused.exactness: Residual as flashinfer (FP32 add, RN to BF16). y uses the deployed input norm_quant arithmetic (FP32 sum order may move y by one BF16 rounding). FP8 x and scales from y: IEEE div.rn absmax/448 and 1/scale, product, cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32 (pre-dispatch: FCHK/MUFU.RCP IEEE division and F2FP.SATFINITE.E4M3; DeepGEMM JIT flags have no fast-math). Top-k: same router kernel, only the id store widens to int64; routed scaling factor 1.0.

fused_gate.change: fused plus one Triton kernel per 64 rows: BF16 tl.dot over K 4096 (8 HGMMA 64x128x16 per 128-wide K step, cp.async 4 stages, 192 KiB shared), logits rounded to BF16, then the router's softmax, lowest-id top-8 and renormalization; ids and weights go to the buffer

removed_per_layer.kernels: nvjet gate 24.6 + zeros 0.9 + router 10.3 = 35.8 us, 2 launches (gaps 3.5 us)

expected_us_per_layer.note: instruction count is about the same as the removed router; most of the gain is launch and latency, hence the extra 5 us/layer selection margin over fused

fused_gate.exactness: Not bit-identical: GEMM accumulation order can move a BF16 logit by one step. Gate: valid top-8 of the FP32 logits within two BF16 steps, ids equal to the router on >= 99% of rows, weights within the BF16-logit rounding bound, sum 1 +- 1e-5.

cpu_checks.triton_interpreter: TRITON_INTERPRET=1, 37 rows in a 40-row buffer: pad slots -1/0, scales bit-identical to the torch IEEE reference, FP8 codes equal to the interpreter conversion of g*(1/scale), router ids and weights (1.2e-7) equal to the torch router, gate-route ids equal on all rows against BF16 logits. The interpreter truncates FP32->BF16 and mis-rounds FP32->E4M3 at binade edges and reads BF16 tl.dot operands wrongly, so those were matched with the interpreter's own conversions and an FP32 dot copy; compiled code uses the cvt instructions listed above.
cpu_checks.selection_gate_with_torch_stand_ins: check_rows passes correct stand-ins; rejects a 2^-20 scale change, a missing pad fill and unnormalized weights (both candidates) and one wrong expert id (fused-gate only).
cpu_checks.pp4_source_check: scripts/check-firmus-pp4-source.py passes on the reconstructed PP4 tree with the overlay

not_candidates.c_input_norm_pair: norm_quant (60.9 us) is the next layer's input add+RMSNorm+FP8, already one kernel; fused_add_rmsnorm (63.9 us) is the post-attention norm, separated from it by MegaMoE: that one is the fused candidate.
not_candidates.d_qknorm_rope: 231-235 MB per 7988-row call (BF16 QKV read 18,432 B/token; FP8 Q 8,192; contiguous and paged K/V 2,048; V image 512) = 57-63 us at 3.7-4.0 TB/s against 130.0 us; per-token time equals EP4 (66 us at 3994). No removable bytes or kernels; layout variants (head4, wide, paired rounding) and the QKV-epilogue fusion were rejected; a latency fix would count at kappa 0.35-0.6.
not_candidates.e_dense_tail: DeepGEMM 0.1.5 heuristic (shared memory 216448/216576 B matches the profile) uses BM256/BN128, cluster 1x2, 3 stages at M=7988: 32 M blocks = 8192 rows, 204 padded rows (2.55%). QKV 2304 tiles = 17.45 waves, O 1024 = 7.76. A tile override needs a DeepGEMM host rebuild; the overlay-only split (7936 + 52 rows) saves one QKV wave (~27 us) but re-reads the 37.7 MB QKV weight in the tail GEMM and leaves O at 8 waves: ~5-12 us/layer at the cap with an unmeasured tail. Not implemented.
